doc.title: Tyner McCoy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Alphonse Mouzon
summary: Tyner describes drummer Alphonse Mouzon as flamboyant, musical and willing to try ideas.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: So I look at your long tenure, a lot of your projects you bring EJ, Elvin Jones back in, there’s that sympatico, that very close relationship you have with him. When I think of Sahara, now you have Alphonse Mouzon.

Yeah (laughs) he was quite a character, he was a good guy. He was a character in a lot of ways, I liked him, he was eccentric, but it was good, he didn’t mind trying things. You know, he’d say, “I got an idea,” he would jump in there and do it, you know, he was very musical in his own way. There were times maybe, I didn’t restrict him but, “Chill here a little bit, we’ll work on it and get it.” He was willing to work with you, he wasn’t the kind of guy that was like, “Well my way is the best way,” he wouldn’t do that in anyway to me, he had too much respect. But he was a nice guy and he worked with Chick and some other people-­
Weather Report, that’s right, Joe Zawinul.
Right, so he had a lot of . . . he was very musical he really was. He was a nice guy he had a lot of respect.
He’s from South Carolina so he’s got to be a nice guy.
Yeah, well my people are from North Carolina.
